A sealed biosphere of up to millions of particles, and all of them live, eat, breed, and die in your browser, simulated on the GPU with WebGPU. Some cells drink the moving light of the tide. Others graze on the photosynthesizers, and others hunt the grazers. Scavengers break down the dead and return them to the water as silt, and from that silt the next generation builds its children. Children mutate into new species. Species that bond grow into bodies: filaments, branched fronds, spirals, packed tissues. Some of these bodies grow beating tails and swim. Every 10 to 18 minutes the climate turns, and the world has to begin again in its own way. It makes its own music, too: each cell sings its species' song, over a chorus of the births, kills, and deaths in view. Leave the simulation running and it keeps changing for hours.

Tidemote is a sealed biosphere of up to millions of particles, and all of them live, eat, breed, and die in your browser, simulated on the GPU with WebGPU. Some cells drink the moving light of the tide. Others graze on the producers, and others hunt the grazers. Scavengers break down the dead and return them to the water as silt, and from that silt the next generation builds its children. Children mutate into new species. Species that bond grow into bodies: filaments, branched fronds, spirals, packed tissues. Some of these bodies grow beating tails and swim. Every 10 to 18 minutes the climate turns, and the world has to begin again in its own way. It makes its own music, too: each cell sings its species' song, over a chorus of the births, kills, and deaths in view. Leave the simulation running and it keeps changing for hours.

How strongly cells of one species bond. Above 15%, each cell keeps up to two same-species partners with springs. Empty slots find the nearest neighbors within bond range; children start bonded to their parent if they are the same species. Bonds last until a partner dies, changes kind, or stretches too far away. Bonds are the links you see and they hold bodies together. Bonded cells share the cost of living (up to 15% less upkeep), shade each other less and are armored against attack. They still pay crowding beyond their bond partners, disperse poorly and their inner cells struggle to reach silt to divide. Species without adhesion are single-celled.
